title: Kyyn is a runtime and design workbench

nodes.summary: Local-first runtime and workbench for a human and their agent
nodes.detail: Kyyn is a local-first runtime and design workbench used by a human together with their existing agent, rather than a hosted service or governance product.

realised.evidence: PR #44 exposes the first local evolution journey through the CLI; PR #49 (seq 46) installs the complete local CLI

nodes.summary: KB owns domain meaning; Kyyn owns loading, execution and acceptance
nodes.detail: The KB owns its domain types, facts, validation, calculations, instructions, tools and views; Kyyn owns loading, execution, discovery, candidates, acceptance and operational integration. KBs may depend on Kyyn to execute.

realised.evidence: KB-authored typed queries/validation run by Kyyn from PR #27-#28; Kyyn-composed evolution acceptance lands in PR #42 (seq 41)

nodes.summary: Exploration is an outcome; preserve unknown and disputed values
nodes.detail: Exploration and improved understanding count as outcomes before reporting or automation exists, and accepted facts may carry unknown or disputed domain values instead of implying 'verified true'.

realised.evidence: A product stance; KB-authored types can model unknown/disputed values but no specific kernel mechanism or PR claims it

nodes.summary: External schedulers call ordinary operations; Kyyn never orchestrates agents
nodes.detail: Schedulers and agent harnesses invoke ordinary Kyyn operations; the kernel does not orchestrate agents itself.

realised.evidence: Negative constraint; no code existed, so nothing orchestrated agents

nodes.summary: No universal ontology or governance engine; effects are not sandboxing
nodes.detail: Rejects a standalone-code requirement, a universal knowledge ontology and a general governance/workflow engine, but also 'just a folder of scripts': the runtime must remove repeated loading, protocol, review and persistence work. Explicit effects aid trusted agents and are not hostile-code containment.

realised.evidence: Mostly negative constraints that the (empty) codebase conformed to; the positive runtime half is delivered across later steps

nodes.summary: Explicitly invoked KB-authored agentic flows allowed; still no autonomous scheduling
nodes.detail: Kyyn does not autonomously orchestrate agents, but KB-authored agentic flows invoked explicitly (ADR 0028) are permitted; they do not turn the kernel into an agent scheduler.

realised.evidence: PR #165 lets explicitly invoked KB tools run Agentic flows with host-supplied model turns; closed recipes run in PR #168 (seq 131)

editorial.note: Desired-state reconciliation: frontmatter replaces Status line, 'proposed in' becomes 'defined in' ADR 0028; no requirement change.

notes: A short, stable product-charter lane with no subsections, split by commitment. 'Boundaries and alternatives' was treated as part of the decision (it is not Context/Consequences/Verification) and yields one mostly-negative node. The only substantive change is seq 122 softening 'Kyyn does not orchestrate agents' to 'not autonomously', carving out explicitly invoked agentic flows; I modelled that as a refine rather than a replace because the no-scheduler commitment survives. Realisation for charter-level nodes is necessarily judgemental (0001.03 unknown).
